overall: At 03:20 ET, Atlanta is sitting at 71.6°F with a running max of 73.4°F and a near-zero warming velocity, consistent with a typical pre-dawn lull. The most striking feature is the extremely narrow temperature-dewpoint spread of just 1.8°F (71.6°F / 69.8°F), indicating a near-saturated, very muggy boundary layer that could act as a damper on afternoon convective heating.
forecast_obs_notes: Model guidance clusters in a 82.3–84.7°F range, with GFS and HRRR agreeing at 84.7°F on the high end while NBM comes in notably lower at 82.3°F and ECMWF splits the difference at 83.1°F. max_temp_prediction: The best estimate for today's TMAX is approximately 82.5°F. The deeply moist airmass evidenced by the near-100% relative humidity at 03:20 ET suggests latent heat demands will resist surface temperature rise more than deterministic models account for, supporting the odd model's better-confidence 81–82°F signal over GFS/HRRR's 84.7°F. Confidence is moderate; the primary risk to the upside is if the boundary layer mixes out more aggressively than expected mid-morning.
